newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt support remains strong - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt support remains strong - poll.

text.p: The Australian government has ended 1996 with its electoral support undiminished since the March 2 election, according to a poll published on Tuesday.

The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found primary vote support for the Liberal-National coalition was at 48 percent, one percentage point above the March result, while Labor was at 36 percent or 2.7 percent below its March result.
Prime Minister John Howard finished the year with 53 percent of the 1,150 voters surveyed saying they were satisfied with his performance.
This compared with 42 percent of voters saying they were satisfied with Opposition Leader Kim Beazley's performance.
The poll also found 53 percent of voters preferred Howard as prime minister, compared to 24 percent who said Beazley would make a better prime minister.
"The Newspoll shows the gap between the parties widening to 12 points, after narrowing to less than 10 points for the first time since the budget earlier this month," the newspaper said.
Howard's dissatisfaction rating was 35 percent, down from 42 percent before the March election, while Beazley's dissatisfaction rating was 36 percent, up from 17 percent.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,150 voters around the country by telephone over the last weekend.
